title: Six Affordable International Trips for the Diwali Long Weekend
excerpt: From Kathmandu from Rs 8,596 to Hanoi, Colombo, Bangkok, Tashkent and Baku, two Diwali guides map six short-haul breaks that fit the Nov. 6-11 festival window — with 'from' fares and full-trip budgets as the sources state them.
body:
• Diwali in our coverage runs Nov. 6 (Dhanteras) to Nov. 11 (Bhai Dooj) — six short-haul destinations fit that window without long-haul fares.
  • Skyscanner 'from' fares cited by Market Dot News start at Rs 8,596 Delhi–Kathmandu, Rs 12,085 Delhi–Hanoi and Rs 12,219 Delhi–Colombo — 'from' prices as listed, not guaranteed fares.
  • Curly Tales puts full-trip budgets under Rs 50,000 per person for all six, lowest for Nepal at Rs 22,000–Rs 35,000 per person.
  • Visa friction is low: no visa for Indians in Nepal, a 30-day exemption for Thailand, and visa-free Malaysia entry for eligible Indian passport holders until Dec. 31, 2026.

With Diwali falling from Nov. 6 to Nov. 11 this year, travellers in India have a six-day window that suits a short international break. A Skyscanner round-up reported by Market Dot News names six destinations where the rupee stretches further, with 'from' flight prices for Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru. Curly Tales prices complete trips to overlapping destinations at under Rs 50,000 per person. Prices below are quoted exactly as those sources state them.

Nepal — the lowest budget and no visa

Best for first-time international travellers and mountain views. Curly Tales estimates Rs 22,000–Rs 35,000 per person, the lowest budget in its list, and notes Indian citizens do not need a visa but must carry an accepted travel document. Skyscanner lists Delhi to Kathmandu flights starting at Rs 8,596, Mumbai at Rs 12,554 and Bengaluru at Rs 13,800, and notes the Nepali rupee is pegged at Rs 1 to NPR 1.6, which makes budgeting straightforward. Start in Kathmandu for Kathmandu Durbar Square, Boudhanath Stupa and its markets, then continue to Pokhara for lakeside cafes and Himalayan views. November is generally favourable for clear Himalayan views, though mornings can be chilly.

Sri Lanka — the most variety in five days

Best for travellers who want coast, hills and heritage in one short trip. Curly Tales estimates Rs 30,000–Rs 42,000 per person. Skyscanner lists Delhi to Colombo from Rs 12,219, Bengaluru from Rs 14,007 and Mumbai from Rs 16,367, at around 3.5 Sri Lankan rupees to the Indian rupee. The island packs in Galle Fort, Colombo, tea country and Ella, with its green hills, hiking trails and the Nine Arch Bridge. Curly Tales warns November weather can be unpredictable because monsoon conditions vary across the island, so build flexibility into beach plans.

Vietnam — street food and the strongest converter story

Best for food-led city breaks. Skyscanner puts the rate at around 271 dong to the rupee and lists Delhi to Hanoi from Rs 12,085, Bengaluru from Rs 18,228 and Mumbai from Rs 20,268. Its picks are pho in Hanoi, lantern-lit evenings in Hoi An, beach time in Da Nang and Phu Quoc, where searches are up 133%. Curly Tales estimates Rs 38,000–Rs 50,000 per person, centred on Hanoi's Old Quarter, Hoan Kiem Lake and a day trip to Ninh Binh or Ha Long Bay. Arrange the Vietnamese visa before departure via the official e-visa portal, and stick to one region to stay under Rs 50,000.

Thailand — the familiar all-rounder

Best for families and groups who want city and beach options. Curly Tales estimates Rs 35,000–Rs 48,000 per person. Skyscanner lists Delhi to Bangkok from Rs 13,540, Bengaluru from Rs 14,531 and Mumbai from Rs 15,236. Indian travellers are eligible for Thailand's 30-day visa-exemption scheme under rules taking effect on Sept. 15, 2026; check the latest entry requirements before departure. Choose one base — Bangkok for temples and street food, or Krabi or Phuket for beaches — rather than squeezing in multiple islands.

Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan — the Central Asia detour

Best for travellers who have done Southeast Asia and want history instead. For Uzbekistan, Skyscanner lists Delhi to Tashkent from Rs 21,424, Mumbai from Rs 22,457 and Bengaluru from Rs 26,268, notes Tashkent is on its Best-value Destinations list with return-flight searches down 30% year on year, and points Indian passport holders to the e-visa option. For Azerbaijan, it lists Delhi to Baku from Rs 20,052, Mumbai from Rs 25,452 and Bengaluru from Rs 25,586, with direct flights from Delhi and Mumbai and e-visa access for eligible travellers. Baku's UNESCO-listed Old City, Maiden Tower, Flame Towers and Heydar Aliyev Center make it a compact city break. Skyscanner lists up to Rs 1,000 off eligible bookings via HappyFares or Paytm Travel with code SKYIND from Oct. 20 to Nov. 15, 2026 — see its Diwali Sale page for terms.

How to choose

Pick Nepal for the lowest spend, Sri Lanka for variety, Vietnam for food and value, Thailand for an easy family break, and Uzbekistan or Azerbaijan at higher 'from' fares. Malaysia, Bali and Cambodia also appear in the Curly Tales list. Book the Nov. 6–11 window early: 'from' fares move with dates and demand.
